issues.problem: No area measure on M ∖ S is built, so the paper's hypothesis 'finite volume' cannot even be stated. 'Cusps have finite area' is proved by transport: E is injective on the strip, maps it onto W_c ∖ {s}, and is a local isometry, and the strip has hyperbolic area 1/c in ℍ. It is not a measure statement on the surface. Neither direction of 'cusps ⇔ finite volume' is built, and the surface statement needs M compact, which the file drops. All of this is disclosed in SCOPE (b), the REPORT hypotheses and notes, and the row stays partial. It is not an avoidable gap for closing the row: the step the paper needs, finite volume ⇒ cusps, is the thick–thin / classification-of-ends argument. Hence minor, not major. The REPORT phrase 'each cusp is proved to have finite area' slightly outruns what is proved.
issues.fix: Optional. In the REPORT, write 'each cusp is the injective locally-isometric image of a strip of hyperbolic area 1/c (no surface measure is built)'. If a later wave builds the area measure on Γ\ℍ (pushforward of volume restricted to a fundamental domain), add the cheap direction: M compact plus cusps implies finite area.

fidelity_summary: take_closed_unit_disc_metric proves every assertion of l.1877–1883: sing(M) = S; tamely singular; a developing map of the branched cover exists and every one is injective; the singular points of M̃ are exactly the points over S, mapped to ∂ℍ; arbitrarily small open neighbourhoods U are homeomorphic to {r<r0} ⊆ 𝔻_∞ with x ↦ apex; D(U) = horoSet(D x, τ), and D(U) is not open in X. It adds the finite-area statement for the cusps. The hypothesis is DEC-81's metric reading with 'finite volume' replaced by 'a hyperbolic cusp at each s ∈ S'. That replacement is disclosed in the module docstring, the checklist, SCOPE (b), the REPORT hypotheses and a question to the author, and the row is correctly partial and unmarked. The other hypothesis changes are weakenings: M need not be compact, the genus is unused, 2g−2+s>0 is unused, second countability is unused. M's T2 / locally path-connected / first-countable / connected instances hold for a surface. The metric notion is not trivialised: it must give the topology, be a length metric and agree locally with d_ℍ in the charts. It is unique (IsHyperbolicMetric.unique) and exists for complete surfaces (the quotient metric). Metric completeness ⇔ Thurston–Goldman completeness is genuinely proved: ⇐ by the quotient metric plus uniqueness, ⇒ by a Hopf–Rinow lifting argument through mathlib's IsLocalHomeomorph.continuous_lift. That direction carries no SLSC hypothesis, because IsCompleteHyperbolic quantifies over it. DEC-55's compact-open definition is not relevant to this file.
